Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification - ZenMed

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we have alignment on the performance qualification for a Private/VPC deployment: 

Summary of requirements (from call):
- Latency target: p95 <= 150ms for single-turn text generation (50 token avg).
- Streaming: client requires server-side streaming with token-level latency <= 100ms for first-burst and steady-state <= 50ms per token.
- Throughput/concurrency: expected steady throughput of ~120 concurrent users (approx 20 rps), peak burst up to 400 concurrent.
- Concurrency model: per-tenant token cache and KV reuse preferred; session affinity during burst windows.

Immediate asks for your network team so Neha and Jordan can size tests:
1) Network path: do you plan VPN (IPSec) or cloud VPC peering? Please attach network diagram and egress flow.
2) Expected egress NAT / public IPs (if any) and burst bandwidth available (Gbps).
3) Internal latency budget: typical internal app-to-Redwood-proxy RTT and variance (p50/p95).
4) Any proxy/load balancer in front of your app that could add TLS termination/idle timeouts.

I've attached a suggested SLO matrix and a sample network diagram template to help (zenmed-slo-matrix.xlsx, zenmed-network-diagram.pdf).

Next steps from Redwood: Jordan will propose a test plan (end-to-end synthetic + streaming test) and Neha will surface any infra blockers for private deployment. Can we target Monday 18th for the network diagram + answers?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: zenmed-slo-matrix.xlsx (Excel, 38KB)
Attachment: zenmed-network-diagram.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@zenmed.ai>

Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2024 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification - ZenMed

Marissa / Jordan —

Thanks for the recap and the templates. Quick answers from our side and attached network diagram. High-level:
- We're planning to use AWS VPC Peering from our primary account (no internet-facing egress for inference traffic).
- Egress: outbound to Redwood will flow via a NAT/egress subnet with two NAT gateways (for HA). We can reserve a small set of Elastic IPs if that helps.
- Burst bandwidth: our VPC has a 5 Gbps NAT gateway baseline; we can provision higher for test windows.
- Internal app-to-proxy RTT (from our app nodes in us-west-2): p50 ~ 8ms, p95 ~ 32ms (based on our internal metrics).
- We do have an internal F5 LB that terminates TLS; it adds ~3-5ms median and can be bypassed for test endpoints if needed.

Attached: zenmed-network-diagram.pdf (internal view) and a short CSV with NAT IPs.

We'll loop in NetOps for the deeper network details — tagging @netops.

Best,
Alex
CTO, ZenMed
Attachment: zenmed-network-diagram.pdf (PDF, 140KB)
Attachment: zenmed-nat-ips.csv (CSV, 2KB)

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification - ZenMed

Thanks Alex — this is helpful. A few clarifying items and what we'll validate during the test window: 

Clarifying questions (quick):
- Are the NAT gateway IPs static for the test window (we prefer fixed IPs to whitelist on our side)?
- Can you confirm whether traffic will be peered privately (no public internet hop) or if egress will traverse an internet NAT (we need to know if public routing affects latency variance).
- For the F5 LB: can you expose a bypass/test URL that terminates TLS at the app (or allow us to run client tests that target the backends directly)?

What Redwood will validate during the synthetic test:
- Cold-start token latency (first token) and steady-state token latency across 10k synthetic requests, measured at client and server side. Target: p95 first-token < 150ms, per-token steady-state <= 50ms.
- Streaming behavior: validate initial chunk <100ms and 95% of subsequent token updates <= 50ms under 20 RPS baseline and up to 50 RPS spike.
- Concurrency/throughput: run a scaled concurrency test up to 400 concurrent sessions to confirm queueing behavior and tail latency.

Proposed test plan / dates:
- Wed Mar 20: baseline synthetic tests at low concurrency (20 concurrent) — measure p50/p95.
- Thu Mar 21: streaming tests and 100-200 concurrency window.
- Fri Mar 22: peak concurrency spike to 400 for short windows (10 minutes) and final report.

We'll need:
- A static egress IP or a narrow CIDR to whitelist.
- A bypass/test endpoint or temporary security rule to avoid LB-induced TLS termination.
- An on-call NetOps contact during test windows (phone or Slack).

Jordan will follow up with the concrete test harness (k6 + custom streaming client) and the expected metrics payload. If that all sounds good, Marissa — can you confirm availability and I'll prepare a short one-pager for NetOps?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
